ids.221:
Traffic reach & livestream traffic quality
+ Livestream traffic reach still has a gap versus the Premium Beauty industry benchmark.
+ Current traffic depends more on longer livestream hours and ads than on organic growth.
+ Traffic quality is not yet stable when scaling: views do not grow in line with impressions.
ids.222: - Heavy scaling of Hour Live & Sessions spreads traffic into off-peak slots.\n- Warming and retention content lacks continuity.\n- Traffic grows fast but its quality is not well optimised yet.
ids.223: - Add pre-live traffic support: restock videos for key products, pain-point content to pull traffic from short videos into the livestream.\n- Improve traffic efficiency per session rather than only maximising impressions; focus on viewer retention and return rate.
ids.224: Traffic reach has reached the industry baseline; the issue shifts to keeping quality while scaling further.
ids.225: - Track whether views grow in line with impressions as scaling continues.
ids.226: - Keep the current scaling pace while gradually shifting from paid to organic traffic to lower marginal cost.
ids.227: Livestream visuals & ability to draw users into the live\n+ The ability to attract clicks into the livestream does not hold steady as traffic expands.\n+ Visuals, opening frame and image experience are not striking enough at large traffic scale.
ids.228: - Traffic is scaled more broadly at each stage, making it hard to keep the live click rate at its initial peak.\n- Visuals and live openings change little between sessions, reducing freshness as impression frequency rises.
ids.229: - Upgrade layout, lighting and camera angles in a Premium Beauty direction.\n- Optimise the live opening (minigame announcement) and thumbnail to draw attention in the first seconds.\n- Stabilise livestream infrastructure to keep image quality throughout long sessions.
ids.230: The ability to pull users into the livestream is better than the industry baseline; keep it when scaling traffic further.
ids.231: - The main risk is ERR declining as traffic broadens; track it monthly.
ids.232: - Keep and rotate thumbnail / opening frame concepts to avoid losing freshness as impression frequency rises.
ids.233: Product showcase experience & ability to draw product clicks\n+ Product showcase and lead-in lack freshness in long lives.\n+ The review experience is not visual enough to highlight product value.
ids.234: - Product demos are not consistent across sessions and hosts.\n- Missing texture close-ups, before-after and lifestyle visuals.\n- Product CTAs lack urgency and value.
ids.235: - Add skin close-ups, product texture and real demos to hold attention longer.\n- Standardise the product consultation script around set/basket strategy.
ids.236: The ability to lead users to click products outperforms the industry; this is a strength to keep.
ids.237: - Track the trend: this metric usually declines as customers get used to an old concept.
ids.238: - Rotate showcase concepts and add new demos before the metric starts to fall.
ids.239:
Conversion efficiency & ability to drive purchases in the livestream
+ Conversion efficiency does not hold steady as traffic and livestream scale grow.
+ The ability to keep session rhythm and guide buying behaviour varies between hosts, especially in long sessions.
+ Combo value and reasons to buy now are not communicated clearly enough.
ids.240: - Consultation quality varies between hosts.\n- Long live flows put pressure on energy and the ability to keep the consultation rhythm.\n- Conversion CTAs are not clearly standardised.
ids.241: - Standardise host guidelines for a premium brand (style, speaking pace, energy, gestures).\n- Coach the consultation flow and attention retention for long sessions.\n- Standardise CTAs to clarify product benefits, combo/routine value and urgency to buy.
ids.242: Conversion is above the industry baseline; prioritise controlled traffic scaling.
ids.243: - Risk: conversion usually drops when traffic grows faster than consultation capacity.
ids.244: - Scale traffic step by step, tracking CTOR after each step before increasing further.
ids.245: Ability to sustain combo conversion outside campaign days\n+ Combo value and experience are not communicated clearly enough to sustain buying on normal days.\n+ Combo and routine consultation is not strong enough for customers to buy full sets instead of single items.
ids.246: - Users are still strongly influenced by incentive pricing and campaign behaviour.\n- Combo performance depends heavily on gifts, vouchers and campaign days.\n- Routine consultation is not strong enough to drive combo purchases on normal days.
ids.247:
- Present combos as a complete care routine so customers can picture how to use them.
- Build combos per specific need / skin condition to increase personalisation.
- Raise perceived value through storytelling about the user experience.
- Optimise the virtual table to clearly highlight each combo's benefits.
ids.248: AOV is close to / above the industry benchmark; reduce dependence on campaigns to hold it on normal days.
ids.249: - Most of the current high AOV comes from combos on campaign days.
ids.250: - Push combos & routine-selling into Daily slots, not only campaign days.
ids.252: - Operating performance falls when live hours are scaled heavily → more volume does not bring matching efficiency.
ids.253: - Scaling every live time slot is reducing operating efficiency.\n- Some slots do not optimise GMV/h but still run long.\n- The Daily baseline has no sustainable growth activity outside campaigns.
ids.254: - Tier the operating strategy by timeline: peak slots focus on conversion push and Ads; off-peak slots prioritise keeping baseline traffic and optimising cost.\n- Standardise live flow, script and product switching to reduce gaps between hosts and slots.\n- Add support for Daily (seeding, co-host) to reduce dependence on campaigns/vouchers.
ids.255: Operating performance grows with scale; keep the pace and track GMV/hour while scaling further.
ids.256: - Make sure GMV/hour does not drop as live hours keep increasing.
ids.257: - Prioritise expanding in the slots and shift types with the highest GMV/hour.
